model.rationale: Polls from mid and late October put Talarico up two to three points on average, prediction markets price him near two-in-three, and his roughly 4-to-1 fundraising advantage plus the wave of anti-Paxton spending outweigh the state's Republican lean. Most raters still call it a tossup, so this stays on the softer edge of Lean D.
model.watch: Late movement on the economy as the top issue, Paxton consolidating Republican voters, or the Libertarian's share in early voting could tip the result either way.
notes: Open seat: John Cornyn (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's open Senate seat has become one of the closest races of 2026. With John Cornyn defeated in the Republican runoff, Ken Paxton carries the Republican banner against James Talarico, and polls from mid-to-late October show Talarico ahead by roughly two to three points, with individual surveys ranging from a one-point Paxton lead to a five-point Talarico lead. Most race raters call it a tossup, though a couple lean Democratic, and prediction markets give Talarico about a two-in-three chance.

Money is a striking asymmetry: Talarico has raised roughly $146 million to Paxton's $22 million, and outside groups have spent heavily against Paxton. Still, Texas's Republican lean keeps the ceiling high for Paxton, and a Libertarian on the ballot adds uncertainty. The race sits just on the Democratic side of lean, but narrowly.
